Members of the public wishing to observe the meeting may do so in one of the following ways:
(1) Turn your TV to Channel 3;
(2) City’s website at http://www.elmonteca.gov/378/Council-Meeting-Videos; or
(3) Call-in Conference (888) 204-5987; Code 8167975.

(1) Call-in Conference Line – comments/questions can be submitted per the instructions at the

6.  SPECIAL MEETING PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING AGENDIZED MATTERS ONLY:

  As provided under Government Code Section 54954.3, this time has been set aside for persons
  in the audience to provide comment or make inquiries on matters appearing on this Special
  Meeting agenda only. Although no person is required to provide their name and address as a
  condition to attending a meeting, persons who wish to address the body are asked to state their
  name and address. Each speaker will be limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may
  not lend any portion of their speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other
  persons. All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the body as a
  whole and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member of the
  body except through the presiding official of the meeting, members of the body are under no
  obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses

  discussion or deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on

  disruptive to the orderly conduct of the proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that

7.  REGULAR AGENDA:

  7.1  Suspension of the Licensing and Sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks for 2020 in
  Light of Covid-19 Pandemic.

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. Suspend the licensing and sale of Safe and Sane Fireworks for 2020 in light
  of Covid-19 Pandemic.

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Maggie Luuteyen – My name is Maggie Luutuyen and I’ll be having 3 children
  attending Arroyo this upcoming year, and 2 in band. I’m asking that you please
  consider issuing the fireworks booth permit as this is the major fundraiser for our
  band which will help keep our band program running.

  Jessica Schoenfeld – As an Arroyo Band Booster for 8 years I know how vital the
  Firework Booth is to the Band program. By canceling this fundraiser you will cost
  the band anywhere between $7400 to $10000, this is their biggest fundraiser.

  2
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of May 19, 2020

The funds we raise are used to pay for the Fall Field Show. Even if the field show
is changed this Fall due to COVID, we still will have to pay for the music. Then
the following year we would be able to reuse the music from this year. Please do
not cost the kids any further disruption to their educational experience. Have they
not paid enough.

Viviana Longoria – I would like to ask that you allow for the permits of safe
firework stands in our city. My son, Mateo, is a member of the Arroyo High
School marching band and every year my husband and I volunteer for their
firework stand. This allows their high school band to raise a majority of their
funding without putting a major financial burden on the families. In addition, these
funds are also helpful for additional staff needed, purchase equipment, and
competition costs. Not allowing the sales will significantly affect not only Arroyo
High School’s band but, also all of our other City of El Monte high school’s
bands, community programs, and non- profits organizations. Allowing these
organizations to sell fireworks will allow us community members to help raise
funds for our community programs and to celebrate our country’s freedom safely
at home. I ask that you please allow and permit the sales of fireworks.

Jeff Cox – Regarding the issue of approving Firework Permits I would like to urge
the Council to conditionally approve the permits and not close off the source of
much needed funding for community organizations. Just as the Council has
taken steps to try to shore up businesses with grants and residents with financial
assistance the sale of fireworks is a financial lifeline for many community groups
and should not be cut unless absolutely necessary. I realize the Council is in an
awkward position of trying to balance safety with the needs of our community but
conditional approval now would be a strong statement from the council in support
of the community groups who live by this fundraising. Covid-19 health and social
distancing guidance is frequently being updated. Conditional approval of the
permits could be given now and would allow for community groups to continue
the planning or organizing process while health guidance continues to evolve. A
date in mid-June could be set to re-evaluate the permit status. This would allow
the council to still fulfill its oversight role while not prematurely removing
fundraising opportunities from the many groups that depend on them. I urge you
to balance caution with hope and conditionally approve the permits.

Joseph Walsh – I understand that the EL Monte City Council is meeting tonight
(Tuesday the 19th) and will be discussing allowing Safe and Sane fireworks in
the city this year. As long time EL Monte residents, my wife and I have always
enjoyed being able to support our local schools and school clubs by purchasing
Safe and Sane fireworks from the TNT and Phantom stands (usually the TNT
stand in the 7-11 parking lot on Santa Anita)... we usually have a small family
gathering and have our own little fireworks show in our driveway. I understand
that this is a new era, with unforeseen complications and social complexities. We
are still weathering out the Safer At Home orders, though things are slowly re-
opening. My hope is that by July we, as Monteros, will be able to be more social
(with appropriate social distancing), and once again sustain the family tradition of
fireworks with a small gathering. The ability to legally purchase Safe and Sane
fireworks both curtails the desire for illegal fireworks and funds the school groups
that have been financially devastated by Covid 19. I am confident that the
fireworks stands can easily function with social distancing, if this is still a

  3
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of May 19, 2020

mandate in July. In a normal year my family draws near to July with anticipation,
eagerly waiting for the day the fireworks stands open. This year that anticipation
is at a fever pitch... we've all been through so much, and the thought of Safe and
Sane fireworks again this July gives all Monteros hope for a new era, a rebirth of
sorts.

Raquel Merlo – We are the Church of God of Prophecy, a church that serves the
community. With great concern we have received the news of a possible
suspension of sale of fireworks due to the Coronavirus. I would like to highlight
the following points: 1. the families of El Monte, whatever the situation, will
celebrate Independence Day because of how important it means. 2. We offer the
community legal and approved products that keep families safe. 3. If we don't
offer the state approved legal fireworks, families will have the tendency to buy
illegal products, which can led to worse consequences. 4. As a Community
Church, the funds raised helps us to offer aid to programs for our youth and
children. 5. We are dependent on the money we raise for those few days to
carry us out for the rest of the year. 6. We will take all precautions to keep
families safe from Coronavirus by submitting to all safety rules. Awaiting a
positive response, we wish you many blessings.

Joel Whisler – I have been a music teacher at El Monte High School for 25
years. We have been operating a fireworks stand for the past 7 years. We
typically profit around $7000 in the 4 day sale. Because of the pandemic, our
choir had to postpone its trip to perform in Honolulu, Hawaii. We are scheduled
to go next spring. We have no other way to make that amount of money to put
towards our trip. If we are not allowed to sell fireworks, most likely, we will have
to cancel our trip. I'm sure for all the non-profit groups that sell fireworks in El
Monte, this is their main, and possibly only source of funds for the coming
year. Barring a major downturn in the pandemic, I urge you to keep the fireworks
sales. Families can enjoy the safe and sane fireworks and the groups can make
the necessary funds to continue to function for the coming year.

Connie Garcia – I am Arroyo High School Band VP. We have been notified that
the firework booth might be cancelled. This really concerns me I understand it is
due to health concerns. However between now and then, I’m sure we can
organize health precautions. Firework booth is Arroyo band biggest fundraiser
that is used to keep the instruments, props, uniforms well maintained. When we
do the fire work booth, I make sure there are no more than 2 people in the booth.
Set the line and add tape on the floor. We can do it it’s possible with good social
distancing and making sure each booth has a schedule of (2) family members
that live in same household to work 4 hour shifts. Please keep us updated our
kids program will be on the edge!

Tricia Soto – Good evening Distinguished Council Members, I am here to remind
you how we are in true need of our fireworks fundraising event and how it affects
our band program here at Arroyo. The fireworks booth doesn't just create sales, it
creates and strengthens community support, while also allowing our new families
to bond with fellow booster parents. I know in this time of uncertainty, it is the
city's goal to keep us all safe and healthy, but cutting this opportunity for not just
Arroyo, but others as well in the community to fundraise would hurt us
enormously. I myself am in healthcare and I am in the line of fire day in and day

  4
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of May 19, 2020

  out. Which is why I understand completely about being safe and wearing proper
  protective equipment (PPE). I can assure you with the guidance from LA County
  guidelines and city guidelines for us to follow, we can have a successful season.
  All these guidelines would be followed as such and with "no cutting corners" that
  could potentially jeopardize our parents or our valued community. Together we
  can do this! We just need to be properly guided and made sure we adhere to the
  guidelines put forth to us. Thank you for your time and consideration.

  Steve Bennett – Tonight you are discussing the possible suspension of the sales
  of Safe and Fireworks by local non-profit groups in the City of El Monte. I would
  like to share with you what TNT Fireworks has done and is currently doing to
  meet the requirements of the County of Los Angeles Health Department and any
  requirements they may have during the time of fireworks sales. As you know, the
  county extended the “Stay at Home” order last week but also continued to relax
  restrictions. Currently, curbside sales are allowed and I am not sure if you can
  cite a more curbside business than Safe and Sane Fireworks sales. The county
  also recognizes door sales for retail businesses as approved (where a customer
  is serviced at a door or window). Again, we fit that model extensively as retail
  customers are not allowed inside the fireworks stands. We have signage and are
  currently working on training stand operators on how to implement those safety
  requirements. We are doing our part to ensure that our stand operators, your
  non-profit organizations, will be following all rules and guidelines in relation to
  COVID-19 at the time the sales will begin.

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  5-0

  Table the Item to June 2, 2020 and direct the City Attorney’s Office to
  prepare an Urgency Ordinance to suspend Safe and Sane Fireworks for
  2020 only and lastly direct the City Manager to engage in conversations
  with TNT and other businesses that are proposed to sell on that day and
  have discussions regarding appropriate regulations and direct the City
  Manager to come up with a mitigation plan for the non-profit organizations.
